activity.target_definition: y = 6 - log10(MIC[uM]); minimum MIC across organisms

config.score_definition: S(P) = alpha * A_tilde(P) - beta * H_tilde(P); LARGER IS BETTER

units.model_predicted_hemolysis: p-dose scale, 6 - log10(D50[uM]); higher = MORE hemolytic

parent_analysis.caveat: model-predicted values only; no experimental measurement is claimed for this peptide by this tool

filters.rationale: protected parent residues C/G/P are structurally load-bearing (disulfide, turn flexibility, helix breaking); forbidden new residues C/P/M/W avoid unpaired cysteine, helix breaking and oxidation-prone sites; the hydropathy threshold removes substitutions that move no design-relevant property

screening.description: every admissible single mutant was scored with the actual ML models; no heuristic coefficients were used

generation_report.size_justification: N is kept near 12-20 so that exact enumeration of 2^N remains feasible, which is what makes an optimality gap measurable; coefficient cost is 1 + N + N(N-1)/2 real model evaluations

report.interpretation: interaction_strength_ratio compares mean |Delta_ij| to mean |Delta_i|. A ratio near zero means the landscape is essentially additive and the problem reduces to independent selection; a larger ratio means the quadratic term genuinely matters, which is what makes this a QUBO rather than a knapsack

qubo.matrix_convention: E(x) = x^T Q x + c with Q symmetric; off-diagonal Q_ij = c_ij/2

build_report.sign_convention: S is maximised biologically; the QUBO minimises its negation, so lower energy means a better predicted candidate
build_report.penalty_strategy: P = penalty_factor * (objective_span + epsilon) = 2.0 * (24.269834 + 0.001) = 48.541668; any penalty strictly greater than the objective span is sufficient because satisfying the constraints costs at most the span (Lucas 2014 principle), and this is then verified by enumeration rather than assumed

landscape_identities.note: the second-order surrogate is exact by construction for |x| <= 2; a failure here indicates an implementation bug, not approximation error

qubo_matrix_vs_polynomial.convention_checked: E(x) = x^T Q x + c, Q symmetric, Q_ij = c_ij/2

lowest_energy_infeasible_assignment.reason: selected 4 mutations, budget is at most 3

penalty_sufficiency.interpretation: passed means every infeasible assignment has strictly higher energy than the best feasible one, so the penalties cannot be out-earned

ising_report.qubit_ordering: Qiskit little-endian: rightmost Pauli character and rightmost measurement bit are qubit 0
ising_report.note: the identity term makes <x|H_C|x> equal E_QUBO(x) exactly; it does not change the argmin

simulator_agreement.note: compared against qiskit.quantum_info.Statevector on the explicit RZ/RZZ/RX circuit; amplitudes are compared modulo a global phase

qubo_optimum_vs_true_best.interpretation: with K <= 2 the surrogate is exact, so this must pass; a failure there would indicate an implementation bug. For K >= 3 a failure is a genuine property of the second-order approximation, not a bug.

exact.uniform_baseline_note: probability that a single uniformly random bitstring is optimal; QAOA success probabilities are reported as a multiple of this

3.interpretation: surrogate_top_pick.true_rank is the metric that matters for optimisation: it is where the selection the QUBO considers best actually lands in the true ML ranking. A rank near 1 means the surrogate is a usable proxy; a rank near out_of means it is actively misleading at this mutation count.

within_budget.note: normalised_rmse is RMSE divided by the spread of the true score differences; a value well below 1 means the surrogate explains most of the variation, around or above 1 means it does not
within_budget.region: 3 to 3 mutations: the feasible region the solvers actually search

beyond_budget.note: normalised_rmse is RMSE divided by the spread of the true score differences; a value well below 1 means the surrogate explains most of the variation, around or above 1 means it does not
beyond_budget.region: 4+ mutations: INFEASIBLE under the budget; reported only to show how the quadratic model extrapolates

exactness_regime.reason: Delta_i and Delta_ij are computed as exact finite differences of the ML score, so the second-order surrogate reproduces the true score identically for up to two selected mutations
exactness_regime.implication: with budget_mode=at_most_k and K<=2 the QUBO is an EXACT representation of the ML landscape over the feasible set, and its optimum is the true best candidate under the models. For K>=3 the surrogate omits third- and higher-order interactions and its fidelity must be read from exhaustive_by_mutation_count.

surrogate_validation.note: the surrogate is exact by construction for 0, 1 and 2 mutations; these figures measure the regime where it is an approximation

verdict.fidelity_within_fixed_mutation_count: MEDIOCRE: within a fixed mutation count of 3 or more, the surrogate's preferred selection lands around the middle of the true ranking, i.e. roughly what picking at random would achieve. The quadratic model carries little usable signal at that size.
verdict.end_to_end_outcome: CORRECT, and for an understood reason: the QUBO optimum is the true best feasible candidate, and it selects only 2 mutation(s), which is inside the surrogate's exact regime. This is a property of this instance, not a guarantee -- had the true optimum required 3 or more mutations, the poor fidelity above would have been load-bearing.
detail: k=3: Spearman=0.516, surrogate's top pick ranks 164/316 by true ML score
verdict.banding: top-pick percentile: >=80 GOOD, >=60 WEAK, >=40 MEDIOCRE, <40 POOR. 50 is what random selection within that mutation count would achieve.
verdict.consequence: the optimisation machinery (QUBO construction, Ising mapping, exact and QAOA solvers) is verified correct independently of this; what is measured here is whether the QUBO faithfully represents the ML landscape, which is a separate question. Because fidelity degrades at 3+ mutations, final candidate ranking is taken from direct ML re-scoring rather than from QUBO energy.
verdict.validity_regime: K <= 2: the QUBO is an exact representation of the ML landscape. K >= 3: the QUBO is a local approximation whose within-size ranking is unreliable for these models.

activity_nearest_identity.meaning: fraction of positions identical to the closest sequence the model was fitted on; high values mean the candidate is an interpolation, low values mean the prediction is an extrapolation

hemolysis_nearest_identity.meaning: fraction of positions identical to the closest sequence the model was fitted on; high values mean the candidate is an interpolation, low values mean the prediction is an extrapolation

activity_prediction_spread.interpretation: standard deviation across bootstrap-resampled models: MODEL/prediction uncertainty, NOT experimental measurement error

hemolysis_prediction_spread.interpretation: standard deviation across bootstrap-resampled models: MODEL/prediction uncertainty, NOT experimental measurement error

pareto.dominance_definition: candidate A dominates B iff A is no worse in both objectives and strictly better in at least one
